messages:
support-jamie: Heads-up — ParcelOne reporting a spike in 504s and timeouts hitting our hosted inference since 11:07 UTC. p95 and tail latencies ballooning. Example req ids: po-9f7a, po-9f8b. Customer is seeing request-level timeouts, not auth/billing.
incidents-bot: Alert: hosted-gateway(us-west-2-gw-3) queue_depth=97% | dequeue_lag rising | continuous-batcher ack_delay > 2s
eng-ava: Thanks. Any traces or a minimal repro payload? Are they hitting a long-seq model or lots of concurrent short requests?
support-jamie: Quick sample from customer ticket:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"open-chat-7b","input":"Summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
```
They say it times out ~10s then returns 504.
sre-linus: Running quick metric pull for gateway dequeues & batcher ack rates.
```
# prometheus-ish
sum(rate(gateway_dequeue_ops[5m])) by (cluster)
sum(rate(batcher_ack_delay_seconds[5m])) by (route)
```
Findings: dequeue_ops flat, ack_delay spiking on routes serving ParcelOne; batch window auto-expanded but workers didn't scale due to thinpool exhaustion.
ops-raj: Looks like a slow-ack spiral: backlog increases -> batcher holds requests longer to fill batches -> ack_delay grows -> queue depth rises -> scheduler defers allocation. Quick mitigation: reduce `batch.window_ms` for the affected route from 20 -> 5 and temporarily cap tenant concurrency.
oncall-maya: I'm going to push the config change to canary in us-west-2-gw-3 now (batch.window_ms=5) and add a temporary 60 req/s tenant cap for ParcelOne. Rolling in ~90s. @eng-ava please stand by for fallback route.
eng-ava: Preparing fallback: route parcelone-fallback -> redwood-small-v2-quant with same interface. Will be ready to switch if the batch window change doesn't stabilize within 5m.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3498765432 | Severity: P2 | Assigned: eng-ava, sre-linus, ops-raj
support-jamie: Customer on the line confirmed an initial drop in 504s after the config change. They still see higher p95 but not repeating timeouts.
sre-linus: Post-change metrics: dequeue_ops up ~20%, ack_delay median down from 2.3s -> 0.6s, queue_depth dropped from 97% -> 58% on canary cluster. Logs show KV-cache priming churn but no auth errors.
ops-raj: Created a short-term playbook: 1) detect ack_delay > 1s for 3m -> auto-shrink batch.window_ms 2) detect thinpool saturation -> scale dequeue workers 3) fallback routing to quantized variant. Will add to runbook.
eng-ava: Pushed fallback route ready. If ParcelOne still hits >1% 504s in next 10m, we'll shift 20% of traffic to quantized variant and monitor.
support-jamie: ParcelOne reports ~80% reduction in 504s and acceptable latency. They've asked for RCA and long-term config suggestions.
oncall-maya: Marking incident as "stabilized" pending 30m of good metrics. Will open a post-incident RFC for safer batching defaults and thinpool autoscale policies.
support-jamie: Closing loop with customer: offered mitigation summary and next steps (RFC + runbook updates). Will reopen if recurrence.
